items.text: Ketchup, pickles, cereal, sock. Ymamot Creation!
items.where: Ymamot Creation: little Amy in the flashback (Grace's voice)
items.script: [gleeful six-year-old announcing a recipe, bossy and proud, quick; Ymamot is said YAH-mah-mott] Ketchup, pickles, cereal, sock. [beat] Ymamot Creation!

items.text: Heading out? I can come. I have a tool belt, a flashlight and a strong opinion about whatever you're about to fight.
items.where: Justin offers to join the party (Gregori house talk)
items.script: [thick New York accent, easygoing, friendly, goofy proud dad] Heading out? I can come. I have a tool belt, a flashlight and a strong opinion about whatever you're about to fight.

items.text: Great. Let me grab my jacket. And the ladder. Don't ask about the ladder.
items.where: Justin joins the party
items.script: [thick New York accent, warm, cheerful, a little distracted] Great. Let me grab my jacket. And the ladder. Don't ask about the ladder.

items.text: No problem. The hallway light won't finish itself. It's been almost done since June.
items.where: Justin when Tom says not right now
items.script: [thick New York accent, easygoing, dry, a little rueful] No problem. The hallway light won't finish itself. It's been almost done since June.

items.text: Somebody has to tag out. I'll wait. I'll be on the ladder.
items.where: Justin when the party is full and Tom must swap someone out
items.script: [thick New York accent, easygoing, relaxed, amused] Somebody has to tag out. I'll wait. I'll be on the ladder.

items.text: Halftime. I have a minute. Let's go.
items.where: Joins the party
items.script: [thick New York accent, warm, easygoing dad, a little distracted, still half watching the game] Halftime. I have a minute. Let's go.

items.text: Hold this. No, the other end.
items.where: Greeting
items.script: [thick New York accent, mildly impatient, hands full, friendly] Hold this. No, the OTHER end.

items.where: Loose Wire, 0.7s, he spots the wire (lw_spot)
items.script: [thick New York accent, spotting something, mild professional alarm, half amused] Who left THIS here?

items.text: Loose wire. Not my problem any more.
items.where: Loose Wire, 1.5s, holds the copper end out (lw_present), jab follows
items.script: [thick New York accent, dry, deadpan, handing the problem over with a shrug] Loose wire. [beat] Not my problem any more.

items.text: Ow. Okay. A little bit my problem.
items.where: Loose Wire, 3.0s, after the spark bites him (lw_drop)
items.script: [thick New York accent, small yelp, then sheepish, shaking the hand out] Ow. [beat] Okay. A little bit my problem.

items.text: Wire nuts! Never have enough of these.
items.where: Wire Nuts, 0s, digging in the pouch
items.script: [thick New York accent, cheerful, mid-project, rummaging in a tool belt pouch] Wire nuts! Never have enough of these.

items.where: Wire Nuts, 1.25s, first underhand throw
items.script: [thick New York accent, quick, bright, calling the color as he throws] Yellow!

items.where: Wire Nuts, 1.87s, second throw
items.script: [thick New York accent, quick, brighter, second throw] Red!

items.where: Wire Nuts, 2.6s, overhand throw
items.script: [thick New York accent, big wind-up, gleeful, the overhand finisher] And BLUE!

items.where: Wire Nuts, 3.85s, the nod
items.script: [thick New York accent, satisfied, matter of fact, a small nod] Color coded.

items.where: Bad Call, 0.15s, on the couch leaning forward
items.script: [thick New York accent, leaning in at the TV, fast disbelief] He was IN.

items.text: ARE YOU KIDDING ME WITH THAT CALL?
items.where: Bad Call, 1.5s, up and pointing, the hit lands at 1.7s
items.script: [thick New York accent, full-throated sports yell at the TV, standing, pointing, rising to a roar] ARE YOU KIDDING ME WITH THAT CALL?

items.where: Bad Call, 3.55s, final yell (bc_yellD)
items.script: [thick New York accent, hoarse, outraged, one last blast with a cupped hand] WHO IS PAYING YOU?!

items.where: Bad Call, 4.5s, sits back down
items.script: [thick New York accent, deflated, muttered, dropping back onto the couch] Unbelievable.

items.where: Fresh Fit, 0s, runway walk
items.script: [thick New York accent, smooth, low, amused at himself] Clear the runway.

items.where: Fresh Fit, 1.25s, collar at 1.26s, sleeve 1.58s, shades on 1.86s
items.script: [thick New York accent, clipped, precise, a checklist with a tiny pause between each word] Collar. [beat] Cuff. [beat] Shades.

items.text: This shirt cost more than your pond.
items.where: Fresh Fit, 3.3s, the pose, dazzle hit at 3.6s
items.script: [thick New York accent, smug, smooth, a wink in the voice, looking down his nose] This shirt cost more than your pond.

items.where: Fresh Fit, 5.2s, strutting away
items.script: [thick New York accent, cool, quiet, over the shoulder] You're welcome.

items.where: Demo Day, 0s, walking in
items.script: [thick New York accent, gleeful, pumped, shouting over the noise] Demo day! Wall's coming down!

items.where: Demo Day, 1.0s, looking up at the wall
items.script: [thick New York accent, sizing it up, dry, a little sinister] Nobody liked this wall.

items.where: Demo Day, 2.45s, first swing, hit at 2.6s
items.script: [thick New York accent, grunt of effort, shouted on the swing] ONE!

items.where: Demo Day, 3.82s, second swing, hit at 3.96s
items.script: [thick New York accent, bigger grunt, shouted, the wall gives] TWO!

items.where: Demo Day, 4.75s, resting on the hammer
items.script: [thick New York accent, breathless, pleased with himself, wiping his brow] Open floor plan.

items.text: Which one of you is it.
items.where: Breaker Flip, 0s, opening the panel
items.script: [thick New York accent, calm, talking to the breaker panel, scanning] Which one of you is it.

items.where: Breaker Flip, 1.4s, finds the breaker
items.script: [thick New York accent, quiet, pleased, finger landing on the switch] There you are.

items.where: Breaker Flip, 2.3s, flips it off, screen goes dark at 2.52s
items.script: [thick New York accent, calm and flat, a statement of fact] Breaker's off.

items.where: Breaker Flip, 3.3s, in the dark, counting on his fingers
items.script: [thick New York accent, whispered in the dark, even, slightly menacing countdown] Three. [beat] Two. [beat] One.

items.where: Breaker Flip, 4.15s, flips it on, lightning at 4.56s
items.script: [thick New York accent, the same calm voice, a held pause before the last word, then a quiet grin] Breaker's... [beat] on.

items.where: Breaker Flip, 5.15s, closing the panel and saluting
items.script: [thick New York accent, dry, a two finger salute, mock professional] Licensed and insured.

items.where: Giant Sneeze, 0.3s, nose twitch
items.script: [thick New York accent, nose twitching, nasal, a warning to everyone] Hang on. Hang on.

items.where: Giant Sneeze, 1.3s, build frames up to the peak at 2.9s
items.script: [thick New York accent, a quick rising build, each ah bigger and higher, breath catching, about one second] Ah... ah... AH...

items.where: Giant Sneeze, 3.5s, the sneeze, sound and gale at 3.54s
items.script: [thick New York accent, a huge explosive sneeze, the loudest thing in the game, full body] AH CHOOOOO!

items.where: Giant Sneeze, 5.65s, the apology wave
items.script: [thick New York accent, small, sheepish, sniffing, polite] Excuse me.

items.where: Foot Tap, 0s, standing there
items.script: [thick New York accent, relaxed, content, a tiny edge of warning] Nobody touch anything.

items.where: Foot Tap, 1.3s, the no-no wave
items.script: [thick New York accent, gentle dad warning, seeing her coming, a little nervous] Rosie. No.

items.where: Foot Tap, the big spread-arms scream frame (held 1.1 s), the hit lands on it
items.script: [thick New York accent, a huge drawn-out scream of pain, arms spread, red in the face, as long and loud as the word allows] OOOUUUCH!!!!!!

items.text: MY FOOT! WHO TOUCHED MY FOOT?!
items.where: Foot Tap, the scream frames after the OUCH, hit already landed
items.script: [thick New York accent, a piercing, high-pitched scream of betrayal, way out of proportion] MY FOOT! WHO TOUCHED MY FOOT?!

items.where: Foot Tap, 4.78s, hopping with the foot in both hands
items.script: [thick New York accent, still screaming, hopping, outraged that a tap could hurt this much] IT WAS SO LIGHT!

items.where: Foot Tap, 5.82s, arms folded, pretending
items.script: [thick New York accent, tight, strained, pretending, voice cracking on the second one] I'm fine. [beat] I'm FINE.

items.where: DRYWALL, 0s, carrying the sheet in
items.script: [thick New York accent, workmanlike, a little strained carrying it, in charge] Everybody behind me.

items.where: DRYWALL, 2.3s, stands the sheet in front of the party
items.script: [thick New York accent, satisfied tradesman, standing it in place] Drywall's up.

items.where: DRYWALL, 3.0s, driving screws
items.script: [thick New York accent, counting under his breath, focused, drill in hand] Four screws.

items.where: DRYWALL, 4.2s, knocks on the sheet
items.script: [thick New York accent, knocking on it, listening, approving] Solid.

items.where: DRYWALL, 5.25s, thumbs up
items.script: [thick New York accent, thumbs up, done, warm and final] Let it dry.

items.where: Takes a hit
items.script: [thick New York accent, offended gasp, protective of the jacket] Not the jacket!

items.text: Somebody turn the game back on.
items.where: Under a quarter HP
items.script: [thick New York accent, tired, bargaining, flat, on one knee] Somebody turn the game back on.

items.text: Tell the basement I loved it.
items.where: Knocked out
items.script: [thick New York accent, dramatic and fading, a little wry] Tell the basement I loved it.

items.text: And THAT is how you close out a game.
items.where: Battle won
items.script: [thick New York accent, triumphant sports-announcer swagger, fist pump] And THAT is how you close out a game.

items.where: Foot Tap, 2.8s, Rose taps Justin's sneaker toe (also Grace when Rose is down)
items.script: [tiny, careful, barely a whisper, mischievous] Tap.

items.where: Foot Tap, 2.8s, Grace taps Justin's sneaker toe when Rose is down
items.script: [tiny, careful, barely a whisper, mischievous] Tap.
